chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding the buying of the Roman women, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy them and sell them.'

key_terms.الرُّومِيَّاتِ: Roman women (specifically female slaves of Roman origin)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying and selling Roman female slaves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of trading female slaves of Roman origin, reflecting the practical economic norms of the early Shia community. The brevity of the report underscores the established consensus on the status of Rumiyyat as valid commodities within Islamic jurisprudence, distinct from other categories of slaves.
